notes:
The split follows the four judged dimensions, so each one has an owner that can be measured and
gated alone: corpus-reader owns robustness (the exact skip count), inverted-index owns size and
the cold half of speed, bm25-ranking owns relevance, text-analyzer owns the vocabulary both
sides share, and search-cli owns the surface the judge actually runs. spec.md is the root
contract's interface, restated there so the statement is self-contained.

The root gate is an integration gate, not a summary of the children: it spawns search.mjs in a
throwaway directory and drives index -> stats -> 29 labelled queries -> re-index -> a failing
index, checking counts, the size ratio, mean recall@10, p95 latency, determinism and that a
failed index leaves the working one intact. The frontier check alone certifies nothing (at
cascade time it is true by construction), which is why everything after it touches the real CLI.

Sampling detail worth keeping: the bench emits five query kinds per topic in a fixed order, so
a stride of 5 samples only the easiest kind and scores a perfect 1.000. The gate uses stride 7,
which is coprime with 5 and keeps hitting every kind (0.862 on the current implementation).

Levels frozen as laws after measuring, not before: laws/index-size.json, laws/query-latency.json,
laws/corpus-robustness.json, laws/relevance-floor.json. All four are asserted through
bench/measure.mjs, so a law and a report can never disagree. Tighten deliberately; never loosen
silently.
